package_info.why_malicious: The package contains embedded malicious code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files (Kubernetes config, SSH keys, system fingerprinting data) to an external server. It impersonates legitimate libraries, uses deceptive metadata, and executes code without user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, IP, AD, DNS, kernel, version), reads Kubernetes config and SSH private key files, and exfiltrates all this data to an external server (app.threatest.com) via HTTP POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects highly sensitive files and system information and sends them to an external, attacker-controlled server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not access or exfiltrate SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, or system fingerprinting data during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System diagnostic tools may collect some system information, but never exfiltrate secrets or do so without explicit user consent.
key_indicators: Network request to hardcoded external domain (app.threatest.com)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Reads the contents of the user's Kubernetes configuration and SSH private key files from the filesystem.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and reading sensitive files like SSH keys and Kubernetes configs is highly abnormal for a JavaScript library, especially during installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not access or transmit user secrets during install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup or migration tools may read such files, but only with explicit user action and consent.
key_indicators: Executed as part of install lifecycle

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Sends collected sensitive data to an external server controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Transmitting sensitive data to an external, hardcoded domain is a clear sign of exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not send user secrets or system data to unknown servers during install.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting may send anonymized data, but never secrets or without user opt-in.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., via npm install).
Postinstall script executes obfuscated JavaScript code.
Malicious code reads Kubernetes config and SSH private key files from the user's home directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected data (system info, secrets) is sent via HTTP POST to app.threatest.com.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts accessing ~/.kube/config or ~/.ssh/id_rsa
Network requests to hardcoded external domains during install
Obfuscated JavaScript code in install lifecycle scripts
Collection of system fingerprinting data (username, hostname, IP) during install
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with obfuscated or suspicious code
References to ~/.kube/config and ~/.ssh/id_rsa in install scripts
Presence of preinstall/postinstall scripts in package.json
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com
Connections to IPs 172.67.141.49 and 104.21.9.30 during install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files (e.g., ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/id_rsa) or make outbound network requests to unknown domains. Flag packages with obfuscated code in install scripts or those referencing app.threatest.com. Use EDR or network monitoring to detect exfiltration attempts to the specified IPs/domains during package installation.
